title: `when/then/otherwise` masks elementwise branches; `&`, `|` and `coalesce` evaluate every operand
verdict: an elementwise branch sees NULL on the rows its condition excludes; other branches, `&`, `|` and `coalesce` run on every row
description: The `when` docstring warns that Polars computes all expressions passed to `when-then-otherwise` in parallel and filters afterwards, so each expression must be valid on its own. The code at py-2.1.0 does better for most branches.

Masking (in memory and streaming): when a `then` or `otherwise` operand is elementwise and is not a bare column or literal, the planner records its input columns, and `TernaryExpr` evaluates it on a frame where those columns are NULL on the rows the condition does not send to it; a branch no row takes is skipped unless needed for broadcasting. The streaming engine keeps an elementwise expression whole in a select node, so the same code runs there. So `pl.when(c).then(x.cast(t))` does not raise on rows `c` excludes; Polars's tests check this on both engines, also for multi-chunk structs (#29799).

Still eager: a non-elementwise branch (aggregations, windows, `map_batches` without `is_elementwise=True`), which both engines compute on every row; every branch under `group_by().agg` or `over()`, where `evaluate_on_groups` runs all three operands with no masking; a branch whose inputs are only literals; and an elementwise branch that turns NULL into a raising value, such as `x.fill_null('bad').cast(t)`.

`coalesce` is an ordinary function whose arguments are all evaluated on every row before it folds them, and `&` and `|` evaluate both sides on every row (in parallel). This is the operand order ST-12 records, and the soundness bug #604.

The raising expressions in Polars are strict casts (polars-cast-int, polars-cast-double-to-int, polars-cast-string), string parsing and temporal errors (polars-temporal-errors); integer division by zero gives NULL and integer overflow wraps (polars-int-divide, polars-int-arith).

To probe: common subexpression elimination descends into ternary branches outside group_by and may hoist a subexpression that occurs twice into a column computed on every row, which would undo the masking; and a strict cast in a `then` branch, a later `coalesce` argument and under `group_by().agg`, on the streaming engine.
reference: The reference evaluates an expression only on the rows its operator sees: a `CASE` branch on the rows that reach it, a filter's condition on the rows below it, a join condition on the pairs it forms. Its issue analysis (`Rel.HasIssue`, `SubstraitLean/Safety.lean`; docs/how-it-works.md) trusts the engine's evaluation order: `CASE` is lazy, `AND`/`OR` are not, and filter and join conditions may run before the filters below them. A plan `verify` reports error-free must run without error, so an engine that evaluates a raising expression on rows outside that model breaks the guarantee. sverify's Polars translation would need its `CASE` written so that a raising branch only sees its rows, or the issue analysis to treat Polars's `CASE` as eager.

evidence.note: #29799: strict cast after masking a struct field
evaluate: a branch with mask columns runs on a frame whose columns are nulled where the condition does not select it; a branch no row selects is skipped unless needed for broadcasting
mask columns: the leaf columns of an elementwise branch that is not a bare column or literal
evaluate_on_groups (group_by agg, over): all three operands on every row, no masking
streaming: an elementwise expression stays whole in a select node, so the same TernaryExpr masks
streaming: a ternary with a non-elementwise operand has its operands lowered to separate streams over the full input
coalesce receives every argument fully evaluated
function inputs (coalesce's arguments) are all evaluated before the call
& and |: both sides evaluated on every row, in parallel
CSE descends into ternary branches outside group_by
engine tests, in memory and streaming: a strict cast in an unselected branch does not raise

provenance.notes: Contradicts the title and verdict. At py-2.1.0 the in-memory and streaming engines mask an elementwise branch: before evaluating a `then`/`otherwise` that is elementwise and not a bare column or literal, they null its input columns on the rows the condition does not send to it, and skip a branch no row takes. So `pl.when(c).then(x.cast(t))` does not raise on rows `c` excludes. Still eager: a non-elementwise branch (aggregations, windows, `map_batches` without is_elementwise), every branch under group_by().agg or over() (evaluate_on_groups), a branch whose leaves are only literals, and an elementwise branch that turns NULL into a raising value (`x.fill_null('bad').cast(t)`). `coalesce` and `&`/`|` evaluate every operand on every row (ST-12, #604 for AND/OR). Lead to probe: CSE can hoist a subexpression that occurs twice, also inside a branch, into a column computed on every row before the select, which would undo the masking. The docstring's warning predates the masking. See the round 2 report for the proposed corrected fact.

evidence.note: masking in evaluate; none in evaluate_on_groups

provenance.notes: Corrected title, verdict and description: round 1 read only the docstring and stated every operand runs on every row; the source reading above shows elementwise branches are masked. Kept the eager cases, `&`, `|` and `coalesce`. Status stays open.

evidence.note: `test_when_then_scalar_condition_masks_unselected_branch`, `engine` in-memory and streaming: `when(lit(False)).then(col('x').cast(Int64)).otherwise(0)` over 'bad', 'worse' is 0, 0 without raising

notes: Pins on both engines that a branch a scalar condition never takes is not evaluated.

Polars's CI runs the unit tests by default, where a lazy `collect()` without `engine` runs the streaming engine (also once with `POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=4`), and again with `POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY=in-memory` (.github/workflows/test-python.yml#L55-L78, #L168-L178); eager `Series` and `DataFrame` calls run in memory. Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), not run.

Streaming agrees with memory: `when(x == '1').then(x.cast(Int64))` does not raise on the masked rows; `&` and `coalesce` evaluate the strict cast on every row and raise on both engines (only the error's counts differ, per morsel); a cast after a filter sees the filtered rows only. The CSE cases are in polars-exec-cse-hoist and PL-6.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each observation (`STREAMING_OBSERVATIONS`, python/tools/sverify_dev/probe_polars.py) with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')` and records both results. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.
